title: The Paralympic Games
article:
Everyone has heard of the Olympics, games of skill and determination that date back to Ancient Greece. More recently in 1960, the Paralympics were established. But what are the Paralympics, how did it start, why do we have them, and what happened in this Paralympic game.

The Paralympics are much like the Olympics with many of the same sports including Archery, Swimming, and Track and Field. The Paralympics however are for people with disabilities, with disabilities from limb deficiency to blindness. This means that the Paralympics has some added sports like Wheelchair Basketball and Blind football. This helps athletes perform in environments that are right for them.

The Paralympics movement first started in 1948 when Sir Ludwig Guttmann organized a sports competition for 16 WWII veterans in England. A few years later The first International Stoke Mandeville Games were held. These games took place every year until 1960, the Ninth Game in Rome. This is considered to be the first Paralympic with 400 athletes and 23 nations taking part in 8 different sports. Every 4 years it was held, new sports were added to the games and more boundaries were broken. The first Winter Paralympics started in 1976.

This Paralympics took place in Paris, and started on the 28th of August and ended on the 8th of September featuring 4,400 athletes who competed in 8 sports. China came home with the most medals at 220, then Great Britain at 124 and finally The United States at 105. Some of the biggest highlights include Jodie Grinham, the first ever Paralympic athlete to win gold while 7 months pregnant. Matt Stutzman, dubbed the armless archer, won his second medal. The U.S women's swim team won 30 medals, 10 of them being gold. Finally the refugee team won its first two medals from Zakia Khudadadi and Guillaume Junior in Taekwondo and Track.

As you can see the Paralympics have come such a long way. They might not be as known as the Olympics but they are just as important. They show the skills of athletics breaking boundaries and making changes.
author: Ava Samuels
